# MarkDKBerry.com

YouTube: [https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry](https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry)

Patreon: [https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies](https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies)

Workflows: [https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows](https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows)

---

This was adapted from a workflow by *"sftawil"* on Discord, and adapted here. Eventually removing the 1st sampler pass and using only the 2nd sampler as a detailer. This worked best of all my tests for detailed results. 

**WHY**? I think because using a fresh run means you are giving the Minimax model a new look at everything. This approach was superior to dual sampler methods I tried. So I will stick with it. It is also fast, considering.

**Updated**: 21st August 2026. *(v18 Fixed issue with dialogue not working causing mouth movement to fail in upscale, renamed, and updated settings node for targetting megapixels.)*

**Use**: **SINGLE PASS LOW DENOISE v2v DETAILER USING MINIMAX H3**


---

## USING THIS WORKFLOW

**Get a structural video made elsewhere, then import it here for detailing.** I am finding 832 or 960 to be as big as it needs to be for structural round before importing here to resize.

**If using audio (dialogue) from video then plug that in to vae audio encoder**, if not then you need to supply an mp3 or music or ambience sound and plug that into the vae audio encoder.

**Set MP (megapixels) based to avoid OOMs, and upscale the video** (see the notes beside the video import node). Size it to fit your VRAM and avoid ooms. 2mp is ideal size but mostly I only manage 1 or 1.2mp.

**I've been leaving the width and height of the actual "H3 Reference To Video Model" Node set to 1mp**. We know it to be the size the H3 model was trained on. But the important bit is the size of your inbound video and what you resize that to.

**Set the length of the video in two places:** 1. the video frame count (inbound video node in frames) and match that in the "duration" node for the "H3 Reference To Video Model", *(even if you get this wrong it seems to still work)*.

**Length of clip vrs output resolution will be defined by where you OOM**. I have extensive notes for my 3060 RTX below, and how I set that is mostly based on clip length. That info is next to the "load video in" node. So use that as reference to figure out yours.

**Make a good prompt, and target the ref images correctly**. 

## ISSUES 

*see [github Model ReadMe](https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows/blob/main/workflows_by_model/Minimax-H3/ReadMe.md) for expanded details of issues and fixes*

- **Fixed: dialogue wasnt working when upscaling with up to v17 of this workflow, it stripped mouth movement out.** This was due to incorrect latent audio connection. It is fixed as of v18. Be aware if you video in has no audio you will now need to provide some for this workflow to run without error. See load audio node for notes. </br>

- **If dialogue audio from video is weak, increase denoise to 0.75**. Also make sure to prompt it as well. otherwise 0.3 to 0.45 can work but sometimes it weakens the audio in and mouth movements needing denoise higher. </br>


- **ClownScheduler was causing ref image characters not to be used**, so have removed it from v18 and will use manual sigmas or the BasicScheduler from now on. I wont be using that node moving forward.

widgets_values:
# INBOUND VIDEO SIZE:

This is where you will oom. so you need to find the sweet spot for your GPU between inbound video size and length of clip.

When you oom, then you need to reduce inbound video size until it fits or reduce the length of the clip.

If increasing inbound video size then I use the best Upscaler I have (RTX nvidia is fast), if I am reducing the inbound video size then I use Resize Image v2 from KJNodes, and set the height to 0, then the width controls the long edge and scales it.

## FRAME LENGTHS VRS ASPECT RATIOS VRS OOMS.

main oom culprits are length vrs aspect ratio. I fix that by changing the "frame load cap" or "skip first frames" to get to what works, if I dont want to change aspect ratio. square aspect ratios oom lower, the below are based on 16:9, and wider you can go higher.

- 241 frames (10 seconds) with 1 image ref: I can do 1504 on long edge takes 20  mins. 3 image refs: 1334 on long edge takes 17 mins.

- 192 frames (8 seconds) best I got (1.2mp took 30 mins with dialogue scene on my 3060 RTX) 

- 124 is roughly 5 seconds (to 2mp takes about 20 mins on my 3060 RTX).

The target video is a realistic interior scene shot from in front of the elevator doors, with warm light catching the marble walls and brass door trim.
[Shot 1] A medium group shot establishes <Subject 1>, the marble lobby with its closed brass-toned elevator doors and carved stone surround directly behind the group. The four figures stand together facing the elevator, waiting: <Subject 3>, the brunette in black leather pants and vest, on the far left; <Subject 4>, the blonde in the blue dress, beside her; <Subject 2>, the man, at center; and <Subject 5>, the Black woman in the leopard-print dress, on the right. 

<Subject 5> (S1) tightens her arms across her chest and says with a sarcastic edge, <d>[English] He's drunk, the asshole.</d> <Subject 3> presses her lips together and shakes her head quietly, saying nothing, her eyes flicking toward the man. At 00:03.000, <Subject 4> (S2) tilts her head with a sarcastic smirk and says sharply,<d>[English] Like you aren't high half the time?</d> 
At 00:05.500, <Subject 5> (S1) snaps back, raising one hand in a dismissive, disdainful gesture, <d>[English] Shut up, bitch!</d>
At 00:07.500, <Subject 2> (S3) lowers his gaze, rubs the back of his neck, and says nervously, <d>[English] I may have had a couple of drinks. I was nervous.</d> His shoulders stay tense as he avoids eye contact with the group until the shot ends.

overall_soundscape:
Quiet room tone with a faint distant elevator mechanism sound continues throughout the shot.

AUDIO IMPORTANT:

if there is no audio in your video-in then it errors. 

If you have silent video, you will need to provide audio in of some kind to run the workflow, even if you dont include it in the output video. Use the audio loader to load in a random mp3 (e.g. 10 seconds of music or ambient silence) and set duration to match your inbound video. swithc the audio vae encoder to use this not the video. This should then work.

NOTE: I found if I prompt for "non_diegetic_music:" it will then use it rather than the audio, so make sure to put "N/A" in any audio descriptors for the prompt if you want to keep the audio you are loading in.

# SIGMAS & DIALOGUE SCENES

I sometimes use res_multistep, simple scheduler, 3 steps and 0.3 to 0.45 for non-dialogue scenes But if I am pushign jup to 0.75 then I get issues with those so use er_sde with beta 57 at denoise 0.75.

I always use er_sde with beta or beta57, denoise 0.75, with dialogue scenes. higher denoise is needed to help drive the lipsync audio from the video back in, else it can weaken it.

## FOR REF CHARACTER IMAGES

- with ref image control you need structure to be applied in the upscaler stages. This means using "simple" scheduler might b best, as it will keep the steps sigmas high and then drop off near the end. start with sigmas higher like 0.45 to push faces into the result. 3 steps should be fine. I also use 0.3.

NOTE: I had an issue with ClownScheduler so no longer use it, it was not making use of the ref image characters so I swapped it out for basic scheduler, or use manual sigmas.


## IF JUST DETAILING NO REF IMAGES

- then you can use other schedulers like "constant" (a straight down diagonal line) is common for upscaling as it is less structural detail and more polish and denoise to suit how strong you want the change. 4 steps will be fine.

## OTHER INFO

you can play around with manual sigmas and test what works best for your situation.
